moments.title: Two pairs of swans
moments.text: The commissioners of New York's Central Park gave Lincoln Park two pairs of mute swans, the start of the zoo. The park commissioners soon began acquiring other animals and building a bear cage, a bison enclosure, a sea lion pool and an animal house.

moments.title: A private nonprofit takes over
moments.text: The zoo became a private institution, run separately from the Chicago Park District, which still pays part of its costs.

moments.title: 150 years
moments.text: The zoo marked its 150th anniversary with a special exhibit on its history.

moments.title: Today: Lincoln Park Zoo
moments.text: The zoo at 2001 N. Clark St is one of the oldest in the country and is still free to visit. Members, donors and visitors pay about 80% of its operating costs.

facts.label: First animals
facts.note: A gift from the Central Park commissioners in New York.

Free admission since opening per a secondary source; private nonprofit since 1995 with a Park District subsidy (zoo's own site). Story confirmed; no changes.
